title: Things to Do in Patna: Bihar Museum, Golghar, Takht Sri Patna Sahib & the Ganga
seoTitle: Things to Do in Patna: Museums, Heritage & Ghats | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Patna: the Bihar Museum and Patna Museum, Golghar and its view, Takht Sri Patna Sahib, the Mauryan ruins of Kumhrar and Agam Kuan, the Ganga aarti at Gandhi Ghat, the Khuda Bakhsh Library, Buddha Smriti Park, Chhath Puja, litti chokha, and trips to Vaishali and Nalanda.
dek: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, the Pataliputra of the Mauryas and Guptas, on the banks of the Ganga.
searchIntent: Travellers spending one or two days in Patna, often as a gateway to Bodh Gaya, Rajgir, Nalanda and Vaishali.
intro: Patna, on the south bank of the Ganga, was Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan Empire under Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka and later of the Gupta Empire. Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador, described its wooden walls in the 4th century BCE. It is also the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

The things to do in Patna include the outstanding Bihar Museum, the old Patna Museum, the beehive-shaped Golghar granary, Takht Sri Patna Sahib, the Mauryan ruins at Kumhrar, evening aarti on the Ganga, and the Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Library. Chhath Puja, in October or November, transforms the ghats. Vaishali and Nalanda are easy day trips.
One to two days is enough. October to March is the most comfortable time.

See the Mauryan ruins at Kumhrar
Watch the Ganga aarti at Gandhi Ghat

items.name: Explore the Bihar Museum
body: The Bihar Museum, opened in 2015 in a striking modern building, is one of India's best museums, with galleries on the region's history from prehistory to the Mauryan, Gupta and Pala periods, Buddhist and Jain art, and Bihar's folk traditions. It is closed on Mondays.

items.name: See the Patna Museum
body: The Patna Museum, in an Indo-Saracenic building from 1917, has fine stone and bronze sculptures, a fossil tree and, famously, a casket said to contain relics of the Buddha. The Didarganj Yakshi, a polished Mauryan-era statue, is now displayed at the Bihar Museum.

items.name: Visit the Khuda Bakhsh Library
body: The Khuda Bakhsh Oriental Library, opened in 1891, holds rare Arabic and Persian manuscripts, Mughal paintings and a manuscript said to have been in Emperor Akbar's collection.

items.name: Climb Golghar
body: Golghar, built in 1786 as a granary after a famine, is a beehive-shaped building with two spiral staircases winding around the outside to the top. The view over the city and the Ganga is excellent, and a light and sound show is held in the evening.

items.name: Visit Takht Sri Patna Sahib
body: Takht Sri Patna Sahib (Harmandir Sahib), in the old city, marks the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh in 1666 and is one of the five Takhts, or seats of authority, in Sikhism. The gurudwara has a museum and serves langar. Cover your head and remove your shoes.

items.name: See the ruins at Kumhrar
body: Kumhrar, in the south of the city, has the excavated remains of a Mauryan pillared hall from around the 3rd century BCE, part of ancient Pataliputra, in a quiet park.

items.name: See Agam Kuan
body: Agam Kuan, an ancient well linked in legend to Emperor Ashoka, stands near a Sitala Devi temple.

items.name: Visit Mahavir Mandir and Patan Devi
body: Mahavir Mandir, a Hanuman temple near the railway station, is one of the busiest temples in Bihar, known for its naivedyam laddus. Patan Devi, in the old city, is an important Shakti shrine.

items.name: Watch the aarti at Gandhi Ghat
body: Gandhi Ghat, where some of Gandhi's ashes were immersed, holds a Ganga aarti on weekend evenings. Boat rides on the Ganga are available from nearby ghats.

items.name: Walk in Buddha Smriti Park
body: Buddha Smriti Park, built for the 2,554th birth anniversary of the Buddha, has a stupa, a museum, a meditation centre and a sapling of the Bodhi Tree.

items.name: See Gandhi Maidan
body: Gandhi Maidan, the city's great open ground, has a tall statue of Gandhi and has hosted many historic rallies.

items.name: Celebrate Chhath Puja
body: Chhath Puja, dedicated to the sun god, is Bihar's most important festival, held six days after Diwali. Millions gather on the Ganga ghats at sunset and sunrise to make offerings standing in the water.

items.name: Eat litti chokha
body: Litti chokha, baked wheat balls stuffed with roasted gram flour, served with a mash of roasted aubergine, tomato and potato, is Bihar's signature dish. Try khaja, thekua and malpua as sweets.

items.name: Visit Vaishali
body: Vaishali, about 55 km north, is linked to the Buddha's last sermon and the birth of Mahavira, with an Ashokan pillar topped by a lion and ancient stupas.

items.name: Go to Nalanda and Rajgir
body: Nalanda's ruins and Rajgir's hills are about 90 to 100 km south-east, a full day trip or an overnight stay.

items.name: See the Sonepur Mela
body: The Sonepur Mela, held in November across the river at the confluence of the Gandak and the Ganga, is one of Asia's largest traditional fairs.

items.name: October to March
body: Pleasant weather; Chhath Puja and the Sonepur Mela in autumn.

items.name: April to June
body: Very hot; visit museums at midday.

items.name: July to September
body: Monsoon rains and a swollen Ganga.

oneDay: Spend the morning at the Bihar Museum, then visit Takht Sri Patna Sahib in the old city. Climb Golghar in the late afternoon and end with the Ganga aarti at Gandhi Ghat.
tips: Patna has an airport and major railway junctions.
Bihar is a dry state; alcohol is prohibited.
Traffic in the old city is heavy; allow extra time.
The Bihar Museum closes on Mondays.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Patna?
faqs.a: Explore the Bihar Museum and Patna Museum, climb Golghar, visit Takht Sri Patna Sahib, see Kumhrar and Agam Kuan, watch the Ganga aarti, visit the Khuda Bakhsh Library and eat litti chokha.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Patna?

faqs.a: Six days after Diwali, in October or November.
